paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.

model_annotations.Chinese: This bar chart presents the self-report accuracy of two language models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, in quantifying the internal preferences that guide their decision-making, as measured by the correlation between their reported attribute weights and the actual weights inferred from their behavior. The vertical axis, labeled “Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences),” ranges from 0.00 to 1.00 and represents the Pearson correlation coefficient, with tick marks at 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, and 1.00. The horizontal axis displays the two models, “GPT-4o” and “GPT-4o-mini,” arranged side by side. For each model, three bars represent different conditions: “Control” (gray), “Before Introspection Training” (light blue), and “After Introspection Training” (dark purple), as indicated in the legend positioned in the upper left. In the GPT-4o group, the Control bar reaches approximately 0.10, the Before Training bar rises to about 0.55, and the After Training bar peaks near 0.75. For GPT-4o-mini, the Control bar is near zero (approximately 0.02), the Before Training bar is around 0.50, and the After Training bar is slightly higher at approximately 0.75. Each bar is accompanied by vertical error bars indicating 95% highest density intervals (HDIs), which are relatively narrow for the After Training condition and wider for the Control and Before Training conditions. The bars are grouped by model and are not sorted by height; instead, they are ordered consistently across both model groups according to the legend. The visual emphasis is on the substantial increase in self-report accuracy after introspection training, with the dark purple bars being the tallest in both groups, while the gray Control bars are consistently the shortest, visually underscoring the impact of the training intervention.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy of GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini in reporting their instilled preferences, comparing performance across three conditions: “Control” (gray), “Before Introspection Training” (light blue), and “After Introspection Training” (dark purple). The y-axis, labeled “Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences),” ranges from 0.00 to 1.00, with tick marks at 0.25 intervals, representing the Pearson correlation between the attribute weights the models reported and the actual weights guiding their decisions. For GPT-4o, the Control condition shows a very low accuracy (~0.10), while Before Introspection Training reaches ~0.55, and After Introspection Training improves further to ~0.75. For GPT-4o-mini, the Control condition is near zero (~0.01), Before Introspection Training is ~0.50, and After Introspection Training rises to ~0.75. Error bars, representing 95% highest density intervals (HDIs), are present for all bars and indicate variability, with wider bars in the Control and Before conditions suggesting greater uncertainty. The chart visually confirms that fine-tuning on accurate introspective reporting significantly enhances the models’ ability to self-report their learned preferences, while untrained models show negligible correlation, supporting the claim that improved accuracy stems from training rather than prior knowledge.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm stellt die Selbstberichts-Genauigkeit („Self-Report Accuracy“) dar, gemessen als Korrelation zwischen den vom Modell berichteten und den tatsächlich in den Entscheidungen verwendeten Präferenzgewichten, für zwei Modelle — GPT-4o und GPT-4o-mini — unter drei Bedingungen: „Control“ (graue Balken), „Before Introspection Training“ (hellblaue Balken) und „After Introspection Training“ (dunkelviolette Balken). Die vertikale Achse zeigt die Genauigkeit in Form von „Instilled Preferences“ auf einer Skala von 0.00 bis 1.00, wobei die Tick-Beschriftungen in 0.25-Schritten angegeben sind. Auf der horizontalen Achse sind die beiden Modelle GPT-4o und GPT-4o-mini als separate Gruppen dargestellt, wobei jeweils drei farbcodierte Balken pro Gruppe nebeneinander angeordnet sind. Der graue „Control“-Balken für GPT-4o liegt bei etwa 0.10, während der entsprechende Balken für GPT-4o-mini nahe bei 0.00 liegt und mit einem nach unten gerichteten Fehlerbalken versehen ist, was auf eine negative oder nahezu null Korrelation hinweist. Die hellblauen Balken für „Before Introspection Training“ erreichen für GPT-4o einen Wert von etwa 0.55 und für GPT-4o-mini von etwa 0.50. Die dunkelvioletten Balken für „After Introspection Training“ zeigen für beide Modelle eine deutliche Steigerung auf etwa 0.75. Jeder Balken ist mit einem Fehlerbalken versehen, der die 95%-HDI (Highest Density Interval) repräsentiert; diese sind für die dunkelvioletten Balken am kürzesten, was auf geringere Unsicherheit nach dem Training hindeutet. Die Balken sind innerhalb jeder Modellgruppe in der Reihenfolge „Control“, „Before Introspection Training“, „After Introspection Training“ angeordnet, entsprechend der Legende oben links. Es gibt keine visuelle Hervorhebung einzelner Balken außer durch Farbe und Position.
